div.l: Right at myn owen cost and be your gyde
And who so will my Iuggement wᵗithsey
Shall pay all that we spend by the wey
And yf ye vouchesauf that yt be so
Telle me anone with out wordes mo
And I will erly shape me therfore
This thing was graunted and our othes swore
Wᵗith full glad hert and prayde hym also
That he wold vouchesauf so to do
And þat he wold be our goủernour
And of our tales Iugge and reportour
And set a soper at a certein pryse
And we will reuled be at his devyse
In hiegh and lowe and þus by one assent
We be accorded to his Iuggement
And there vp on the wyne was fet anone
We dronke and to rest went ecchone
Wᵗith out ony lenger tarying
A morow when the day gan spryng
Vp roos our hoste and was our aller cok
And gadred vs to gider on a flok
And forth we ryden a litell pace
Vn to the wat̉eryng of seint Thomas
And there our host bygan his hors arest
And seide lordes herkeneth yf yow lest
Ye wote our foreward yf ye it recorde

l.hi: Yf evesong and morow song accorde /

div.l: Late se now who shall telle the first tale
As eủer mote I drynke wyne or ale
Who so be rebell to my iuggement
Shall pay for all þᵗat is by the wey yspent
Now draweth cut or we ferther twynne
For he yᵘ hh shortest shall begynne
Sire knight qduod he my meister and my lord
Now draweth cut for this is myn accord
Comthe nere qduod he my lady Prioresse
And ye sire clerk late be your shamefastnesse
Ne studieth nought lay hand to eủery man
Anone to drawe eủery wight began
And shortly to telle as it was
Were it by auenture or sort or cas
